- The **Platforms** page now has a heading per manufacturer (Nintendo, Sega, Sony, Microsoft...), taken from the family the server gives each platform. ## What's new in v0.6.3

### New Xenia options (Xbox 360)
Settable per platform or per game under **Emulator options**, with the emulator's default shown:
- **Controller input:** SDL (PlayStation and most other pads), XInput (Xbox pads, or pads that Steam / DS4Windows make look like one; Windows only) or Automatic. Automatic reads every input system at once, which **doubles the input** when Steam Input or DS4Windows makes a PlayStation pad look like an Xbox pad as well. That showed up as laggy steering and a stick stuck full left or right (seen in Project Gotham Racing 3). Choosing SDL or XInput avoids it.
- **Stick dead zone:** None, Small (5%), Medium (10%) or Large (20%), for both sticks.
- **Controller vibration:** on or off.

body:
## What's new in v0.6.0

### Several accounts (servers and users)
- **Menu → Accounts** lists the RomM users saved on this computer. **Add account** (another user, or another server), switch to one, or remove one.
- The signed-in account's **profile picture** (the one set in RomM, or its first letter on a colour) and name now show at the right of the top bar. Click it to open the list.
- Each account has its **own settings, library, play history, play stats, saved progress and local saves**. The emulators, and a server's downloaded games, firmware, soundtracks and covers, are **shared**, so two users on the same server download a game once. Window mode and update choices are the same for every account.
- **Updating is safe:** whoever is signed in becomes the first account and keeps every file exactly where it was.
- Emulators that keep a game's save inside their own folder (Dolphin, PCSX2 and others): when another account plays the game, the first account's save is **set aside in its own folder and put back** when it plays again, so one account's progress is never uploaded to another's server.
- Removing an account deletes only its own data. Downloaded games and the emulators are kept, and your RomM server is not changed.

### Discord status
- **Menu → Discord status** (off by default, set per account) shows what you are playing on your Discord profile: **Playing RomM Client**, the game, the platform and emulator (for example *Sega Mega Drive/Genesis on RetroArch · Genesis Plus GX*) and how long you have been playing. It disappears when the game closes.
- The Discord desktop app has to be running on the same computer. If it is not, the game is not affected; it is looked for again every 15 seconds while a game runs, and comes back if Discord restarts.

### Fixes and smaller changes (since v0.5.1)
- A resume point made with one RetroArch core is no longer offered to another core after you switch a game's emulator (it could crash). Every core now files its progress on the server under its own name, such as `retroarch-genesis_plus_gx`; older saves are still recognised.
- A game's **Options** menu has **Delete local save** (a backup is kept) and **Remove downloaded game**.
- If an emulator closes straight away or exits with an error, a **closed unexpectedly** box shows the exit code, what the emulator printed and the usual causes.
- The selected game's highlight is no longer cut off on wide windows.

## Installing
**Windows:** run `RommClient-Setup-0.6.0.exe`, then choose **Normal** or **Portable**. If you already have v0.5.4, **Menu → Check for updates** offers this version.
**Linux:** download `RomM-Client-0.6.0-x86_64.AppImage`, make it executable and run it.
Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## What's new in v0.5.2

### Switching emulators no longer offers the wrong save
- After changing a game to a different emulator or RetroArch core, the **Saved progress** question no longer offers the previous core's resume point. It could not be loaded by the new core (and made RetroArch crash). The game now starts fresh, and the earlier core's saves on your server are left untouched.

### Delete local save / Remove downloaded game
- A downloaded game's **Options** menu has two new rows:
  - **Delete local save** removes this computer's saved progress for the game (a backup is kept; the server's copy is not touched).
  - **Remove downloaded game** frees the disk space; the game downloads again when played and its saves are kept.
  - Both ask first.

### When an emulator fails
- If an emulator closes straight away or exits with an error, a **closed unexpectedly** box now shows the exit code, anything the emulator printed and the usual causes, instead of just returning to the game page. Pressing **Stop game** never shows it.

### Fixes
- The update notes dialog follows the new pointer behaviour (the controller highlight is not overridden by a resting mouse pointer).

## What's new in v0.5.1

### A proper "Now playing" screen
- The dialog shown while a game runs is now a **full-window Now playing screen**: the game's **cover** in a ring that breathes while you play (a letter tile until the cover loads), its name and what plays it (for example `RetroArch · Genesis Plus GX`), and **chips** for the platform, the emulator and whether it is resuming (`Resuming where you left off`, `Resume point on`/`off`) and that your saves sync to your server.
- Tiles show **this session's clock** (it stops when the game closes), the game's **total played** time and **when it was last played**, from your RomM play history.
- A **stage line** follows what is really happening: emulator started, playing, then saving progress, all the way through to *Sending your progress to the server…*. The screen stays up through the save upload and goes away by itself when it is done.
- The controller quit buttons are shown as key caps (**Back + Start**, or **Share + Options** on a PlayStation pad), and there is a **Stop game** button for the mouse.

### Controller and mouse
- **The mouse pointer is hidden while a controller is in use** and comes back when you move the mouse.
- A pointer resting on a button or menu row **no longer overrides the highlight** in dialogs, menus and the on-screen keyboard.

### Updates
- The update question now shows the **full release notes in a scrollable area** (Up / Down or the mouse wheel; LB / RB a page), laid out with headings, bullets and space above and below lists, instead of a cut-off summary.

body:
## What's new in v0.5.0

### Choose the emulator, per platform or per game
- Press **Y / F4 / Triangle** on a platform or a game and choose **Emulator**. Only emulators that can really play that system on your computer are listed: for example a Mega Drive game can use RetroArch with **Genesis Plus GX** (the default), **PicoDrive** or **BlastEm**; a Wii game can only use Dolphin. A game follows its platform unless it has a choice of its own, and the row says which.
- **Saves and resume points belong to the emulator** (and for RetroArch, to the core, since two cores keep them in different formats). Changing the emulator of a game that has progress, on this computer or on your server, **warns you first**. Nothing is deleted: switch back and your progress is there again. RetroArch's usual core keeps the save folders and server name it always had, so nothing already saved moves.

### Emulator settings without knowing the command line
- Every emulator now has **Emulator options** (switches and lists), per platform and per game: resolution, graphics API, aspect ratio, vertical sync, screen layout, sound and more. Some are command-line switches (Dolphin, Xenia, fast boot); others are written into the emulator's own settings file just before it starts (PCSX2, DuckStation, Azahar, RPCS3, RetroArch, PPSSPP, melonDS, Cemu, xemu).
- **The emulator's own default is shown** (`Default: 1x (native)`), and marked in the choice list, so you know what "default" means. A game shows what it inherits from its platform and where it differs (`4x · this game (platform: 2x)`).
- A value chosen for one game never leaks into the next: when a later game chooses nothing, the emulator's default is put back. Settings you change inside an emulator yourself are left alone.
- **Extra arguments** (free text) for anything else, per platform and per game, with `=`, `-`, `"` and `\` keys on the on-screen keyboard (Shift gives `(` and `)`). Text in quotes keeps its spaces, and your text goes before the game on the command line.
- **Azahar** gets the options behind most "runs badly" reports: **graphics API** (OpenGL / Vulkan), **sound emulation**, **sound output** (including *No sound* to see whether sound is the cause) and the sound timing switches.

### A "Playing" dialog instead of minimising
- The window now stays where it is while a game runs, with a dialog that names the game and the emulator and says when it is starting, playing and closing, so there is always an answer on screen. It has a **Stop game** button, and reminds you of the controller quit buttons (hold Back + Start, or Share + Options).

### Improvements
- Menus size to their content and wrap long values, so nothing is cut off; values on a highlighted row are readable; the on-screen keyboard wraps long text.
- Text arguments now go before the game on the emulator's command line (several emulators only accept the game as the last argument).
- A platform's emulator override is now checked: an emulator that can't play the platform is ignored instead of being launched.

## Installing
**Windows:** run `RommClient-Setup-0.5.0.exe`, then choose **Normal** or **Portable**. If you already have v0.4.0, **Menu → Check for updates** offers this version.
**Linux:** download `RomM-Client-0.5.0-x86_64.AppImage`, make it executable and run it.
Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
name: RomM Client v0.5.0

body:
## What's new in v0.4.0

### Updates are built in
- **The app now checks for new versions** when it starts (in the background) and from **Menu → Check for updates**. When one is available you see what it brings and can **Download and install**, **Remind me later** (nothing again until a start-up at least 6 hours later) or **Ignore this version**.
- Downloads are checked against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`. On Windows the installer upgrades your copy in place (a portable copy stays portable) and the app starts again; on Linux the AppImage is replaced and started again. Your data is not touched.
- The check only asks GitHub for the list of releases in the public [RomM-Client-Releases](https://github.com/stevejackson80/RomM-Client-Releases) repository; nothing about you or your library is sent.

### Linux is now a single AppImage
- The Linux download is `RomM-Client-<version>-x86_64.AppImage`: make it executable and run it. No install step and no root, so it works on SteamOS too. Your data stays in `~/.local/share/RomM-Client` (set `ROMM_DATA_DIR` to keep it elsewhere). The old tarball and `install.sh` are gone.
- **Xenia Canary (Xbox 360) now works on Linux.**

### Resume points are your choice
- Resume points (picking up exactly where you stopped) can be switched **on or off per platform and per game**. They are on by default where the emulator officially supports save states (RetroArch, DuckStation, PCSX2); where it doesn't, the option says why it isn't available. A game's own saves (memory cards and the like) always sync.
- **Azahar (3DS)** no longer uses save states (its developers say they are only for short-term use); only the game's own saves sync, shown as one "In-game save".
- **Cemu (Wii U)** saves now sync, and its "Getting started" window no longer appears.

### Fixes
- **Dolphin:** GameCube saves now sync (Dolphin adds the game's region to the memory card's file name, which the app was not watching).
- **melonDS:** controller buttons are now set up for you (PlayStation and Xbox-style pads), and the DS user is named after your player name.

## Installing
**Windows:** run `RommClient-Setup-0.4.0.exe`, then choose **Normal** or **Portable**.
**Linux:** download `RomM-Client-0.4.0-x86_64.AppImage`, make it executable and run it. On a Steam Deck, in desktop mode, use **Add to Steam**.
Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

Upgrading from an earlier version: Windows, run the new installer over the old one; Linux, run the AppImage (the old install can be removed with `~/.local/opt/RomM-Client/install.sh --uninstall`, which keeps your data unless you say otherwise).
name: RomM Client v0.4.0

body:
## What's new in v0.3.0

### Wii games are playable with a gamepad (Windows and Linux)
- **Wii Remote and Nunchuk on your controller.** A Wii game now starts with an emulated Wii Remote with a Nunchuk already mapped to the controller you're using (Xbox, PlayStation, Steam Deck, Switch Pro...):

| Wii | Controller |
|---|---|
| A / B | A (south) / right trigger or B (east) |
| 1 / 2 | X / Y |
| - / + / Home | Back / Start / Guide |
| D-pad | D-pad |
| Nunchuk stick / C / Z | left stick / left shoulder / left trigger |
| Shake the Remote | right shoulder |
| Shake the Nunchuk | click the left stick |

- **Choose how the pointer works, per game.** Open a Wii game's options (**Y / F4 / Triangle**) and pick **Wii pointer**:
  - **Right stick**: moves the cursor like a mouse, on any controller (click the stick to recentre). This is the default.
  - **Motion**: point by moving the controller, like a real Wii Remote (needs a pad with motion sensors, such as a PlayStation pad).
  - **Motion, left/right reversed**: the same, with left and right swapped, for a pad whose sensors report the other way round.

  The choice is remembered for that game on this computer and can be changed at any time.

### Improvements
- The game options button and menu are now both labelled **Options** (the footer used to say "Progress", which hid the new setting).

## Installing
**Windows:** run `RommClient-Setup-0.3.0.exe`, then choose **Normal** or **Portable**.
**Linux:** extract `RomM-Client-0.3.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` and run `./install.sh` (`--portable [folder]` and `--uninstall` are available). On a Steam Deck, install in desktop mode and use **Add to Steam**.
Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Known limitations
- The Windows installer isn't code-signed, so SmartScreen will warn on first run.
- On Linux, the standalone emulators (and Dolphin and RPCS3) have been checked for install, launch and where they keep their data, but not yet played on real hardware with a gamepad. Xenia (Xbox 360) isn't available on Linux.
- Wii: games that need the Remote tilted or swung (steering by tilting, for example) have no dedicated mapping yet. Motion pointing has been tried with a PlayStation 4 pad only.
- There are no resume points for Dolphin, Cemu, RPCS3 or Azahar on Linux.
- Soundtracks: only MP3s stream while downloading; FLAC, Opus and M4A aren't supported yet.
name: RomM Client v0.3.0

body:
## What's new in v0.2.0

### More emulators on Linux
- **Standalone emulators now install on Linux** from their official AppImages: **DuckStation, PCSX2, PPSSPP, melonDS, Azahar, Cemu and xemu**, plus **Dolphin** and **RPCS3** (below). Each keeps all of its settings and data inside its own install folder, so nothing is written to your home folder.
- PS1, PS2, PSP, DS, 3DS, Wii U, Xbox, GameCube, Wii and PS3 now pick the standalone emulator on Linux; the retro consoles still use RetroArch.

### Dolphin (GameCube and Wii), Windows and Linux
- Official AppImage on Linux, same download feed as Windows.
- GameCube pad 1 is mapped to your connected controller, using Dolphin's own gamepad bindings.
- **Saves sync**: each GameCube game gets its own memory card file, and a Wii game's save folder is found from the game ID on its disc (ISO, WBFS, RVZ, WIA, CISO).

### RPCS3 (PS3), Windows and Linux
- **Games kept as a single ZIP** are unpacked once (the ZIP is then removed to save space) and started from their game folder. ISOs and PlayStation Store folders work too.
- **The firmware installs itself**, silently, the first time (from the PS3 firmware on your RomM server), with a clear message if it's missing or rejected.
- **Controller mapping** for player 1 through RPCS3's SDL handler, kept in its own `romm` profile so your own RPCS3 profiles are untouched.
- **Saves sync** per game, matched by the game's title ID.
- RPCS3's "exit?" question and other confirmation boxes are switched off, so a game closes cleanly from a controller.
- The first time a game starts, RPCS3 compiles shaders for a couple of minutes; this is normal.

### Fixes and improvements
- Fixed a rare failure when a soundtrack download finished at the exact moment the player opened it.
- Windows installer: the Portable install now offers optional Start menu and desktop shortcuts.
- The release workflow now adds the installers to a release you have already written, keeping your notes.

## Installing
**Windows:** run `RommClient-Setup-0.2.0.exe`, then choose **Normal** or **Portable**.
**Linux:** extract `RomM-Client-0.2.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` and run `./install.sh` (`--portable [folder]` and `--uninstall` are available). On a Steam Deck, install in desktop mode and use **Add to Steam**.
Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Known limitations
- The Windows installer isn't code-signed, so SmartScreen will warn on first run.
- On Linux, the standalone emulators (and Dolphin and RPCS3) have been checked for install, launch and where they keep their data, but not yet played on real hardware with a gamepad. Xenia (Xbox 360) isn't available on Linux.
- Dolphin: Wii games need a Wii Remote mapping, which isn't set up yet. A GCZ disc image can't be read cheaply, so its saves aren't synced.
- There are no resume points for Dolphin, Cemu, RPCS3 or Azahar on Linux. A PS3 game whose save folders aren't named after its title ID isn't covered.
- Soundtracks: only MP3s stream while downloading; FLAC, Opus and M4A aren't supported yet.
name: RomM Client v0.2.0

body:
## What's new in v0.1.1

- **Windows portable install: optional shortcuts.** The portable installer now offers optional **Start menu** and **desktop** shortcut checkboxes (unticked by default). Portable copies have no uninstaller, so these shortcuts are not removed if you delete the folder. Silent installs: `/PORTABLE=1 /TASKS="portablestartmenu,portabledesktop"`.
- **Soundtrack streaming fix.** Fixed a rare failure when a soundtrack download finished at the exact moment the player opened it, which could stop an MP3 from playing while it downloaded.
- **Release process.** The release workflow can now attach the installers to a release that already exists, and gives a clear error if the GitHub CLI is missing on the runner.

## Installing

**Windows:** run `RommClient-Setup-0.1.1.exe`, then choose **Normal** (per-user, Start menu entry and uninstaller, data in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RomM-Client`) or **Portable** (any folder, data in a `data` folder beside the program).

**Linux:** extract `RomM-Client-0.1.1-linux-x64.tar.gz` and run `./install.sh` (no root needed; `--portable [folder]` and `--uninstall` are available). On a Steam Deck, install in desktop mode and use **Add to Steam**.

Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Known limitations are listed in the [v0.1.0 notes](https://github.com/stevejackson80/RomM-Client-Releases/releases/tag/v0.1.0): the Windows installer is unsigned, and on Linux only RetroArch games can be played so far.
